js.lean: Charlotte -2.5 is about fair against our blended +3.0, so there is no real edge on the side or the 227.5 total; this is a pass unless a prop is clearly mispriced.

js.lean: No game-side lean: our ratings have MIN by 2 while the market has CLE -4.5, but the samples are tiny and Edwards' status is unresolved, so I'm leaving the market line alone.

MIN's rating is opponent-adjusted net +5.9 after 3 games (raw 121.0 scored / 97.7 allowed). CLE's is +0.5 after 2 games. Those samples are far too small to justify a 6.5-point gap from the market.
MIN is on a back-to-back and Anthony Edwards (28.7 pts, 31.3 min) is questionable with a knee issue. The market likely already prices both, and I have no numbers showing it misses.
Total: our 229.9 against the market 231.5 is a 1.6 gap, inside noise. Both teams play fast (MIN 104.4, CLE 105.4) and take about 40-43% of shots from three, which fits a total near the market.
MIN's shot-quality edge is small: matchup expected points/shot 1.106 against CLE's 1.079 (league 1.084). MIN also leads on offensive rebounding (ORB% 0.361), but CLE has just 2 games of data.
risks: Edwards' status decides the spread and many props. The market will move if he is ruled out or confirmed.
MIN's 3-0 record includes wins by 23, 22 and 25, which probably overstates its true strength. CLE's 2 games include a loss at PHI.
The back-to-back could cut MIN's minutes or effort, but I have no measured effect in the data.
matchups: CLE allows forwards +10% on threes per minute, which helps the Kuminga and McDaniels three-point props. This is a 2-game sample.
MIN allows centers +7% on threes and +9% on assists. That is a mild note for Jarrett Allen, and it is a small sample.
MIN allows guards -11% and forwards -12% on threes, which is a mild negative for Mitchell, Harden and Watson (small sample).

Whether other MIN rotation players are rested on the back-to-back.
